title: Complexity preserved by coin-tape conversion
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite probability space and let $p$ be a public-coin finite-message protocol over shared randomness $\Omega$, with inputs in $X,Y$ and output type $\alpha$. For every $\delta\in\mathbb R$ with $\delta>0$, the protocol over a coin tape produced by converting $p$ with slack $\delta$ has the same communication complexity as $p$.
hypotheses_covered: A public-coin finite-message protocol $p$ over $\Omega$, with inputs $X,Y$ and output type $\alpha$
replaced:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite probability space, and let $p$ be a public-coin finite-message
protocol over shared randomness $\Omega$ with input sets $X$, $Y$ and output type
$\alpha$. For every real number $\delta > 0$, the coin-tape conversion of $p$ at slack
$\delta$ yields a length $n$ and a finite-message protocol over $\mathrm{CoinTape}(n)$
whose communication complexity equals the communication complexity of $p$.
